chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Ibn Mahbub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding a man who ordered his slave to kill a man, and he killed him. He said: So he (the Imam) said: The master shall be killed for it.

key_terms.أَمَرَ عَبْدَهُ: Ordered his slave — the act of commanding an instrument to commit murder
key_terms.السَّيِّدُ: The master/owner — legal principal responsible for the slave's commanded actions
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ السَّيِّدُ: The master shall be killed — legal ruling applying qisas (retributive justice) to the instigator

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when a master orders his slave to commit murder?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a legal ruling that when a master orders his slave to kill a person and the slave carries out the killing, the master bears criminal liability and is subject to the death penalty (qisas). This ruling establishes the principle that one who instigates or commands a killing is legally equivalent to the direct perpetrator in terms of capital punishment, ensuring that the powerful cannot evade accountability by using subordinates as instruments of crime.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who ordered his slave that he should kill a man, so he killed him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The master should be killed due to it’.
